_version-5.5.0:\n\n5.5.0\n=====\n\n:release-date: 2025-03-31\n:release-by: Tomer Nosrati\n\nCelery v5.5.0 is now available.\n\nKey Highlights\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nSee :ref:`whatsnew-5.5` for a complete overview or read the main highlights below.\n\nRedis Broker Stability Improvements\n-----------------------------------\n\nLong-standing disconnection issues with the Redis broker have been identified and\nresolved in Kombu 5.5.0, which is included with this release. These improvements\nsignificantly enhance stability when using Redis as a broker.\n\nAdditionally, the Redis backend now has better exception handling with the new\n``exception_safe_to_retry`` feature, which improves resilience during temporary\nRedis connection issues. See :ref:`conf-redis-result-backend` for complete\ndocumentation.\n\nContributed by `@drienkop <https://github.com/drienkop>`_ in\n`#9614 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9614>`_.\n\n``pycurl`` replaced with ``urllib3``\n------------------------------------\n\nReplaced the :pypi:`pycurl` dependency with :pypi:`urllib3`.\n\nWe're monitoring the performance impact of this change and welcome feedback from users\nwho notice any significant differences in their environments.\n\nContributed by `@spawn-guy <https://github.com/spawn-guy>`_ in Kombu\n`#2134 <https://github.com/celery/kombu/pull/2134>`_ and integrated in Celery via\n`#9526 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9526>`_.\n\nRabbitMQ Quorum Queues Support\n------------------------------\n\nAdded support for RabbitMQ's new `Quorum Queues <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/quorum-queues>`_\nfeature, including compatibility with ETA tasks. This implementation has some limitations compared\nto classic queues, so please refer to the documentation for details.\n\n`Native Delayed Delivery <https://docs.particular.net/transports/rabbitmq/delayed-delivery>`_\nis automatically enabled when quorum queues are detected to implement the ETA mechanism.\n\nSee :ref:`using-quorum-queues` for complete documentation.\n\nConfiguration options:\n\n- :setting:`broker_native_delayed_delivery_queue_type`: Specifies the queue type for\n  delayed delivery (default: ``quorum``)\n- :setting:`task_default_queue_type`: Sets the default queue type for tasks\n  (default: ``classic``)\n- :setting:`worker_detect_quorum_queues`: Controls automatic detection of quorum\n  queues (default: ``True``)\n\nContributed in `#9207 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9207>`_,\n`#9121 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9121>`_, and\n`#9599 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9599>`_.\n\nFor details regarding the 404 errors, see\n`New Year's Security Incident <https://github.com/celery/celery/discussions/9525>`_.\n\nSoft Shutdown Mechanism\n-----------------------\n\nSoft shutdown is a time limited warm shutdown, initiated just before the cold shutdown.\nThe worker will allow :setting:`worker_soft_shutdown_timeout` seconds for all currently\nexecuting tasks to finish before it terminates. If the time limit is reached, the worker\nwill initiate a cold shutdown and cancel all currently executing tasks.\n\nAUTHORS.txt\nMakefile\nTHANKS\n_ext\n_static\n_templates\nchangelog.rst\nchangelog_formatter.py\ncommunity.rst\nconf.py\nchangelog-1.0.rst\nchangelog-2.0.rst\nchangelog-2.1.rst\nchangelog-2.2.rst\nchangelog-2.3.rst\nchangelog-2.4.rst\nchangelog-2.5.rst\nchangelog-3.0.rst\nchangelog-3.1.rst\nchangelog-4.0.rst\nchangelog-4.1.rst\nchangelog-4.2.rst\nchangelog-4.3.rst\nchangelog-4.4.rst\nchangelog-5.0.rst\nchangelog-5.1.rst\nchangelog-5.3.rst\nchangelog-5.4.rst\nchangelog-5.5.rst\nindex.rst\nwhatsnew-2.5.rst\nwhatsnew-3.0.rst\nwhatsnew-3.1.rst\nwhatsnew-4.0.rst\nwhatsnew-4.1.rst\nwhatsnew-4.2.rst\nwhatsnew-4.3.rst\nwhatsnew-4.4.rst\nwhatsnew-5.0.rst\nwhatsnew-5.1.rst","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5f0a0a7a-349c-4b52-9964-568ca6542f81","uuid":"bfe7c8ef-c625-48e2-bcaa-114fba4b4267","timestamp":"2026-11-17T06:59:29.273Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":".. available.\n\nKey Highlights\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nSee :ref:`whatsnew-5.5` for a complete overview or read the main highlights below.\n\nRedis Broker Stability Improvements\n-----------------------------------\n\nLong-standing disconnection issues with the Redis broker have been identified and\nresolved in Kombu 5.5.0, which is included with this release. These improvements\nsignificantly enhance stability when using Redis as a broker.\n\nAdditionally, the Redis backend now has better exception handling with the new\n``exception_safe_to_retry`` feature, which improves resilience during temporary\nRedis connection issues. See :ref:`conf-redis-result-backend` for complete\ndocumentation.\n\nContributed by `@drienkop <https://github.com/drienkop>`_ in\n`#9614 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9614>`_.\n\n``pycurl`` replaced with ``urllib3``\n------------------------------------\n\nReplaced the :pypi:`pycurl` dependency with :pypi:`urllib3`.\n\nWe're monitoring the performance impact of this change and welcome feedback from users\nwho notice any significant differences in their environments.\n\nContributed by `@spawn-guy <https://github.com/spawn-guy>`_ in Kombu\n`#2134 <https://github.com/celery/kombu/pull/2134>`_ and integrated in Celery via\n`#9526 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9526>`_.\n\nRabbitMQ Quorum Queues Support\n------------------------------\n\nAdded support for RabbitMQ's new `Quorum Queues <https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/quorum-queues>`_\nfeature, including compatibility with ETA tasks. This implementation has some limitations compared\nto classic queues, so please refer to the documentation for details.\n\n`Native Delayed Delivery <https://docs.particular.net/transports/rabbitmq/delayed-delivery>`_\nis automatically enabled when quorum queues are detected to implement the ETA mechanism.\n\nSee :ref:`using-quorum-queues` for complete documentation.\n\nConfiguration options:\n\n- :setting:`broker_native_delayed_delivery_queue_type`: Specifies the queue type for\n  delayed delivery (default: ``quorum``)\n- :setting:`task_default_queue_type`: Sets the default queue type for tasks\n  (default: ``classic``)\n- :setting:`worker_detect_quorum_queues`: Controls automatic detection of quorum\n  queues (default: ``True``)\n\nContributed in `#9207 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9207>`_,\n`#9121 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9121>`_, and\n`#9599 <https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/9599>`_.\n\nFor details regarding the 404 errors, see\n`New Year's Security Incident <https://github.com/celery/celery/discussions/9525>`_.\n\nSoft Shutdown Mechanism\n-----------------------\n\nSoft shutdown is a time limited warm shutdown, initiated just before the cold shutdown.\nThe worker will allow :setting:`worker_soft_shutdown_timeout` seconds for all currently\nexecuting tasks to finish before it terminates. If the time limit is reached, the worker\nwill initiate a cold shutdown and cancel all currently executing tasks.\n\nAUTHORS.txt\nMakefile\nTHANKS\n_ext\n_static\n_templates\nchangelog.rst\nchangelog_formatter.py\ncommunity.rst\nconf.py\nchangelog-1.0.rst\nchangelog-2.0.rst\nchangelog-2.1.rst\nchangelog-2.2.rst\nchangelog-2.3.rst\nchangelog-2.4.rst\nchangelog-2.5.rst\nchangelog-3.0.rst\nchangelog-3.1.rst\nchangelog-4.0.rst\nchangelog-4.1.rst\nchangelog-4.2.rst\nchangelog-4.3.rst\nchangelog-4.4.rst\nchangelog-5.0.rst\nchangelog-5.1.rst\nchangelog-5.3.rst\nchangelog-5.4.rst\nchangelog-5.5.rst\nindex.rst\nwhatsnew-2.5.rst\nwhatsnew-3.0.rst\nwhatsnew-3.1.rst\nwhatsnew-4.0.rst\nwhatsnew-4.1.rst\nwhatsnew-4.2.rst\nwhatsnew-4.3.rst\nwhatsnew-4.4.rst\nwhatsnew-5.0.rst\nwhatsnew-5.1.rst","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01KQUDM36zPapqF4VssHeQP6","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

But, most\n        important, it will also be caught in WorkController.start() to initiate the warm shutdown process.\n        - SIGTERM will also be handled in WorkController.start() to initiate the warm shutdown process (the same).\n        - If REMAP_SIGTERM is set to \"SIGQUIT\", the SIGTERM signal will be remapped to SIGQUIT, and the cold\n        shutdown process will be initiated instead of the warm shutdown process using SIGTERM.\n        - If SIGQUIT is received (also via SIGINT) during the cold/soft shutdown process, the handler will cancel all\n        unacked requests but still wait for the soft shutdown process to finish before terminating the worker\n        gracefully. The next time the signal is received though, the worker will terminate immediately by force.\n\n    So, the purpose of this handler is to allow waiting for the soft shutdown timeout, then cancel all tasks from\n    the MainProcess and let the WorkController.terminate() to terminate the worker naturally. If the soft shutdown\n    is disabled, it will immediately cancel all tasks let the cold shutdown finish normally.\n\n    Args:\n        worker (Worker): The worker that received the signal.\n    \"\"\"\n    safe_say('worker: Hitting Ctrl+C again will terminate all running tasks!', sys.__stdout__)\n\n    # Replace the signal handler for SIGINT (Ctrl+C) and SIGQUIT (and possibly SIGTERM)\n    install_worker_term_hard_handler(worker, sig='SIGINT', callback=during_soft_shutdown)\n    install_worker_term_hard_handler(worker, sig='SIGQUIT', callback=during_soft_shutdown)\n    if REMAP_SIGTERM == \"SIGQUIT\":\n        install_worker_term_hard_handler(worker, sig='SIGTERM', callback=during_soft_shutdown)\n    # else, SIGTERM will print the _shutdown_handler's message and do nothing, every time it is received..\n\n    # Initiate soft shutdown process (if enabled and tasks are running)\n    worker.wait_for_soft_shutdown()\n\n    # Cancel all unacked requests and allow the worker to terminate naturally\n    worker.consumer.cancel_all_unacked_requests()\n\n    # Stop the pool to allow successful tasks call on_success()\n    worker.consumer.pool.stop()\n\n\n# Allow SIGTERM to be remapped to SIGQUIT to initiate cold shutdown instead of warm shutdown using SIGTERM\nif REMAP_SIGTERM == \"SIGQUIT\":\n    install_worker_term_handler = partial(\n        _shutdown_handler, sig='SIGTERM', how='Cold', callback=on_cold_shutdown, exitcode=EX_FAILURE,\n    )\nelse:\n    install_worker_term_handler = partial(\n        _shutdown_handler, sig='SIGTERM', how='Warm',\n    )\n\n\nif not is_jython:  # pragma: no cover","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01AYhg8T4WRrLpW4HU1Stgvz","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

tasks in the group. Alternatively, it causes Celery to execute more tasks\n    # that were previously present in the previous task in the group.\n    # The solution is to be careful and never mutate the options dictionary\n    # to begin with.\n    # Here is an example of a canvas which triggers this issue:\n    # add.s(5, 6) | group((add.s(1) | add.s(2), add.s(3))).\n    # The expected result is [14, 14]. mutate the options dictionary, the result\n    # in this case is [16, 14].\n    # To avoid deep-copying the entire options dictionary every single time we\n    # run a chain we use a ChainMap and ensure that we never mutate\n    # the original `chain` key, hence we use list_a + list_b to create a new\n    # list.\n    if use_link:\n        return ChainMap({'chain': None}, options)\n    elif
